<!-- pr-reviewer: 321df3947e03c5a4ce47f9f2336438ad43136607 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One small test-portability fix is needed; the post logic itself looks right. **Merge order: #1002 first, then this PR.** Retarget this PR to `main` before #1002 merges (AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack").

I built and tested this PR together with #1002 in one worktree: this head (`321df394`) trial-merged with current `main` (`e0cb0049`, v0.18.0). The merge was clean.

### What looks good
- **Same law in all six cycle posts** (fanuc, haas, mazak, tormach, doosan-dnm, sinumerik). `chainRapid` swallows only rapids that stay on the hole (its XY, at or below R). The first rapid that leaves the hole writes `G80` and then posts as the stream says, so the posted traverse and exit are the verified path's own hop and clearance rapids. Heidenhain and Carvera are untouched; they already post their links explicitly.
- **Retract mode.** `G99` is stated when each group opens (fanuc, haas, mazak, tormach, doosan-dnm). The once-per-program `G98`, which was read with the tool already on R, is gone. Sinumerik writes no return word and relies on the seat, which matches what it did before.
- **Cycle cancel.** `G80` is written on every way out of a group:
  - a leaving rapid (`chainRapid`);
  - a new group or a seat (`cycleSeat`, `onCycle`);
  - section end (`endPreamble`), which also covers a tool change.

  I found no path that leaves a cycle active across a rapid, a tool change or a section end.
- **Nothing posts lower than before.** Every changed traverse is the stream's own rapid. The `synth_*` change is a real improvement: the old program read `G98` at the contour floor (Z-6) and positioned XY at that depth before `G82`. It now climbs to R first.
- **Golden diffs: all read.** Every changed line is one of:
  - a `G98` -> `G99` swap;
  - a `G99` / `G80` cycle re-arm or cancel;
  - a stream rapid that used to be swallowed;
  - the modal `X50 Y40` hole re-posted as a full block after its seat;
  - a Sinumerik N-number shift (`M9` / `M5` / `M2` / `G53` lines that moved only by N).

  No GOTO, sub-program or N-targeted jump appears in any changed golden.
- A cut that leaves the hole inside a group is now refused by name instead of being swallowed.
- `cycle_hop.rs` runs one read-back checker on all six posts and checks the checker itself against the #994 program.
- The app test edits are justified: `posting.rs` (`G99`), `doosan_dnm_post.rs` (that stream's swallowed feed is now refused, so the stream gained a chain), and `inverted_support` (the hole is anchored on its first cut).
- The `.cps` changes are clean-room: they cite only RS-274 / ISO 6983 cycle semantics. CPS files are exempt from the 400-line rule. No `unwrap` / `panic!` outside tests.

### Local results (merged with main, Windows, `core.autocrlf=true`)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| post lib, axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, mch_head_search, post_engine, recorded_streams | ok |
| `script_*` x11 (including the six new `drill_retract` goldens) | ok 9/9 each |
| `cycle_hop` | **FAILED 2/3** (see below) |
| app, 30 suites (details below) | all ok |
| clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-post --all-targets`, and `-p camcraft-app` lib plus the touched tests | clean |

App suites with test counts: arc_planes 8, carvera_post 4, conformance 6, doosan_dnm_post 7, drill_prior 12, drill_prior_kinds 4, drill_rplane 8, drilling_axial 7, fanuc_post 11, golden_cl 25, heidenhain_block_form 5, heidenhain_cycles 11, inverted_axis_display 5, inverted_equivalence 2, inverted_post 15, inverted_probe 9, posting 17, probe_dialects 13, probe_tormach 7, program_comments 4, recorded_post_streams 2, setup_post_options 10, sinumerik_safe_retract 3, solid_law_goldens 1, tap_sim 2, tapping_mode 4, tormach_end_units 7, tormach_machines 6, tormach_post 10, tormach_safe_retract 4.

```
---- a_cycle_anchored_on_the_rapid_to_r_is_seated_first stdout ----
thread 'a_cycle_anchored_on_the_rapid_to_r_is_seated_first' panicked at crates\post\tests\cycle_hop.rs:231:5:
the recorded anchors moved: update this variant
```

### Requested before merge
1. **`crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs:216-218` (`drill_retract()`) and `:231`.**
   - **Problem:** the test reads the recorded stream raw and searches for `" AT 1\n"`. The stream is not pinned to LF in `.gitattributes`, so a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` (the maintainer's machine) has `" AT 1\r\n"`. The assert fails, and the seat-path pin is never exercised on that checkout.
   - **Reproduce:** on Windows with autocrlf on, run `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test cycle_hop`.
   - **Fix:** normalise line endings the way #1002's runner does (`.replace("\r\n", "\n")` in `drill_retract()`). Better still, add `crates/post/tests/recorded/** text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes`.
   - **Check:** I converted the stream to LF locally (not pushed) and all 3 `cycle_hop` tests passed. The seat law itself holds on all six posts.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- **Two cycle records with no rapid between them.** `cycleSeat` positions XY at the current Z, which is R after a `G99` hole, so such a stream traverses at R. That is what such a stream says, and the generator always writes the chain plus a leaving rapid. A legacy or foreign stream would still post an R-level traverse, though. To close that case, you could refuse it or seat to the section's `RetractPlane`.
- `onProbeMove` and the protected probe moves do not set `seatKnown`, so a cycle after probing in the same section would not be seated. I don't think the generators produce that today.
- In `inverted/{fanuc,haas}_x.nc` the rapid to R is now a diagonal from the contour exit (Z5) to the hole at Z2. It is the fixture stream's own rapid, so it is the verified path, but it is a shallower approach than before.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not a process file, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is needed.
- The lathe face-drilling exit is filed separately as #1011. Thanks for splitting it out.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Merge order: #1002, then this PR, then #1072. Retarget each child PR to `main` before its parent merges.

This is a delta re-check from `321df394`. I built and tested it together with #1072 (stacked on this PR) in one worktree: #1072's head trial-merged with current `main` (`a6bd69d8`). The merge was clean.

### What changed since the last review
- One commit, `25cbac81`, touching only `crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs`. `drill_retract()` now normalises line endings (`.replace("\r\n", "\n")`), as the recorded runner does.
- This fixes the earlier blocker. No `.cps` file and no golden changed since `321df394`, so the post review from last time stands.

### Local results (Windows, `core.autocrlf=true`)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cycle_hop` | ok on this checkout. Run on #1072's head it was 7/7: your 3 tests plus #1072's 4. |
| every other `camcraft-post` suite, including the 11 `script_*` suites | ok |
| 29 app suites that post, drill or probe (conformance, posting, golden_cl, fanuc/tormach/doosan posts, probe_*, drill_*, inverted_*) | all ok |
| clippy `-D warnings` on post (all targets) and app (lib + touched tests) | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- The two seat gaps noted last time are closed by #1072, reviewed separately.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/**` still has no `eol=lf` attribute. All readers now normalise line endings, so this is only a safeguard for future tests.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
